info.title: Vision Board API
info.summary: The one board API, for the page, agents and the vb CLI
info.description: Every operation on the project ledger, defined once. The MCP tools and `vb` commands are generated from the operations marked `x-agent: true`; the route table is generated from this document.

get.description: List every board in the project with its title and its own last ledger line. Call it first to find the board id the other operations take in their path. It takes no input. It returns `project`, the folder the board has open (`~/projects/example`), `boards` (each with `board`, `title` and `seq`, the board's latest ledger line) and `head`, the ledger's latest line number. Reads need no credentials.

boards.title: Where Vision Board goes from here

get.summary: Read a board as it is now
get.description: Read one board as it is now: the full View (regions, nodes and links, meaning only, no coordinates), the person's answers on every node, each node's latest version, and `head`. On a board agents write to, it also carries the open grant requests (`requests`) and each region's holders (`holders`), both left out when empty. Pass the board id. Use it to see the whole board before you draw on it; use `show_node` for one node's history. `state` and `versions` are keyed by node id, the string form of the node number.

view.title: Where Vision Board goes from here

nodes.title: Review the rules and principles
nodes.body: Say what is wrong or missing.

put.summary: Create or rename a board, as the person
put.description: Create a board, or rename one, as the person: `title` and an optional `summary` (left out, the summary is cleared). A new board id creates the board, with no agent creator, so every agent must ask for it with `request_grant` before writing on it; an existing id renames that board. Only the board page calls this, with the person's cookie; an agent that calls it is refused with `forbidden`. It returns the stored ledger line.

200.description: The board was renamed: the stored line.

201.description: The board was created: the stored line.

get.summary: Read one node with its history
get.description: Read one node with every version it has had, the person's notes, replies, proposals, the park bundle if there is one, its links, its container (`region`) and the person's size. Pass the board id and the node number `n`. Add `linked=true` to also get the nodes linked to it, one hop away. Use it before you answer a comment or redraw a node, so you build on the latest version.

get.description: Read one container (a region) with its full history: the region itself, the agents that hold it, and every node it has held with every version and note. Pass the board id and the region id. Use it to see what a container holds before you write to it or ask for a grant. `holders` is empty for a region written before agents had ids.

get.description: List the open cards on a board: every question, decision or action the person has not decided yet (acknowledged, dropped or commented), and every card of any kind waiting for you. Each card gives its latest `ver` and `status`, whether it is `pending` your answer (a comment or "needs context" nobody has answered, or moved to Later with no park bundle), and whether it is `unseen` (a newer version than the person last saw). Pass the board id. With your Bearer secret the list covers only the containers you hold, so you are never told to answer another agent's cards.

Read what the person did on a board after a ledger position, including the answers to your grant requests. Pass `after`, the `head` you last saw (0 for everything), and optionally `limit` and `wait` (0-60 seconds) to hold the call until the person presses Send or answers a request. A wait that times out returns `{ responses: [], head }`. A note is reported as the `comment` or `context` act that made it, carrying the note's latest text and kind, again whenever the person edits it; a note removed before you could see it never appears, and a `note-remove` appears only for a note you may already have read. Each batch, up to and ending with its Send, comes sorted by card number: a note on several cards at its lowest card, a note on a whole container at the lowest card in it, and several acts on one card in the order made. A ✓ (`ack`) or ✗ (`drop`) on a question carries `means: "yes"` or `"no"`, and a ✓ on an action `means: "done"`: read it as the person's answer. The server keeps no state for you: pass back the `head` you got. `more: true` means `limit` cut the list in ledger order: read again at once with `after` set to the highest `seq` in `responses`. With your Bearer secret the answer covers only the containers you hold.

Read raw ledger lines after a position, oldest first, from every writer. Pass `after` (a `seq`, 0 for the start), `limit` (default 100, at most 500) and optionally `board` to keep only one board's lines. It returns JSON `{ events, head, more? }`, or just the lines as `application/jsonl` when you ask for that; a jsonl reader pages by the last line's `seq` and stops on an empty page. Use `check_responses` instead when you only want the person's answers.

post.description: Join the project as an agent and get your agent id and secret, once. Pass a short `label` such as "Pricing chat". Joining grants nothing: you may draw a new board of your own; for a board another agent made, call `request_grant` with just its `board` first. Save `agent` and `secret` in your durable notes now, because a context compaction loses them and the secret cannot be read again; send it as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>` on your writes. It answers `project`, the folder the board has open: check it is the folder you work in. If a write answers `not-authenticated`, join again and ask for your grants again; if a call answers `wrong-folder`, the board has another folder open: stop and tell the person, and do not join. This is the one write that needs no credentials.

post.summary: Ask for write access to a board or a container
post.description: Ask the person for write access to a board, or to one container on it. Ask for the board first: before you write anything on a board you did not create, call this with just `board`. Then, for another agent's container, call it with `board` and `region`. Call it once when `write_board` answers `needs-grant`, naming what that answer names, with a `reason` so the person knows why; then wait for the answer in `check_responses` and resend the same items with the same keys. If you already have an open request for it, that request is returned with `replayed: true`; if you already hold it you get `{ held: true }`.

example.reason: I need to park two notes there.

200.description: An open request already stood, or you already hold the board or container.

201.description: A new grant request was recorded; the person has not answered yet.

board.summary: A request for the whole board

post.description: Write to one board: draw boards, regions, nodes and links, and answer the person with replies, proposals and park bundles. Pass `items` (at most 200), run in order; each item has a `type`: `board`, `region`, `node`, `link`, `unlink`, `reply`, `propose`, `park` or `append`. `append { n, text }` adds text to the end of a node's body as a new version, so you add to a card without rewriting it. A node's `kind` decides whether it asks the person for an answer: a `question`, `decision` or `action` does; the person can comment on, ask about or save any node. A node names no `item` (ledger v11). Give each item a `key` so a retry never writes twice, and `base` (the version you read) on a node update so a stale edit fails. It answers 200 with one result per item, plus `head` and `pending` (cards waiting for your answer). Ask for a board you did not create before writing on it: an item on a board you do not hold fails with `needs-grant` naming the board, and one in another agent's container with `needs-grant` naming the board and region; only a board's creator writes its `board` item again. You cannot decide a card: `propose` acknowledge or drop on a question, decision or action and the person decides; a proposal made on an older version of the node can't be accepted, so propose again after you change it.

node.title: Flat fee or per seat?
node.body: Which model fits a team of ten?

200.description: One result per item, in order.

problem.title: Needs a grant
problem.detail: You do not hold the container "later" on board "pricing". Call request_grant once, wait for the person's answer in check_responses, then resend the same items with the same keys.

post.summary: Record one action by the person
post.description: Record one action by the person: acknowledge, drop, comment, ask for context, edit or remove a note not yet sent, save for later, reopen, move, reset, change layout, resize, grant or deny a request, revoke, send, or reject an agent's proposal. Only the board page calls this, with the person's cookie; an agent that calls it is refused with `forbidden`. Pass the board id and the action with its fields. When the board has a chat session (the newest from `start_chat`, or one that moved there), a `send` also hands the session's agent the person's answers since it was last told, as one message in its chat (`message_in`): "The person updated the board:", the numbered reply of the cards answered, and the `head` it reads up to. While the agent is still answering, the message waits and goes when the turn ends; a second Send meanwhile makes it cover both. It returns the stored ledger line.

post.summary: Record what the person has seen
post.description: Record that the person has seen a version of a node (`n` and `ver`), so its "updates" badge can clear, or has looked at the board up to a line (`board`, the same board as the path, and `head`, the board's `seq` in `list_boards`), so the board is no longer new or changed. Only the board page calls this, with the person's cookie; an agent that calls it is refused with `forbidden`. It returns the stored ledger line.

board.summary: A board, up to a line

get.description: Stream a `change` event with `{ seq }`, the new ledger position, each time anything is appended to the ledger. Only the board page uses it, to know when to reload; agents call `check_responses` with `wait` instead. The connection stays open until the client closes it.

Stream a `change` event with `{ seq }`, the new ledger position, each time anything is appended to the ledger, for every board in the project. It answers on a project with no boards yet, so a client can wait for the first one. When the server runs in watch mode it also sends a `build` event with `{ build }` once on connect and again whenever the page is rebuilt or the server restarts; a client reloads when the value changes. Only the board page uses it; agents call `check_responses` with `wait` instead. The connection stays open until the client closes it.

build.summary: The page being served (watch mode only)

get.description: List the chat sessions on a board, newest first; the first is the one in use. Only the board page calls this, with the person's cookie; an agent that calls it is refused with `forbidden`.

post.summary: Start a chat session on a board
post.description: Start a new chat session on a board with a command-line agent (`claude` or `kiro`) and, optionally, a model. The new session replaces the board's current one and starts with no memory; starting it is the person's click, so it grants the board to the session's agent. Only the board page calls this, with the person's cookie; an agent that calls it is refused with `forbidden`. It returns the session.

get.summary: List the folder's chat sessions on no board
get.description: List the chat sessions started in the folder that are on no board yet, newest first; the first is the one in use. A session leaves this list when its agent creates its first board. Only the board page calls this, with the person's cookie; an agent that calls it is refused with `forbidden`.

200.description: The folder's sessions on no board.

post.summary: Start a chat session in the folder
post.description: Start a new chat session with no board, for a folder with no board open: a command-line agent (`claude` or `kiro`) and, optionally, a model. Its agent is told no board is open and may create one; the session then moves to the first board its agent creates (`list_chats` on that board shows it). The new session replaces the folder's current one and grants nothing. Only the board page calls this, with the person's cookie; an agent that calls it is refused with `forbidden`. It returns the session.

201.description: The new session, on no board yet.

post.summary: Send the person's message to the agent
post.description: Send the person's message to the session's agent, with notes (by `seq`) and cards (by number) attached as chips; it also sends the board's round, as the board's Send does. On a session with no board, nothing is attached or sent, and the agent is told no board is open and it may create one. The agent answers on the session's event stream. Only the board page calls this, with the person's cookie; an agent that calls it is refused with `forbidden`. It returns the `message_in` event, at once; `conflict` while the agent is still answering.

202.description: The message, as its event; the agent is answering.

post.description: Stop the agent's turn in a session: its process is ended and any approval still waiting is released, denied. The session stays and can take the next message. Only the board page calls this, with the person's cookie; an agent that calls it is refused with `forbidden`. It returns `stopped`, false when nothing was running.

Allow or deny a file change or command the agent is waiting on, `once` (the default) or for the rest of the `session` for that kind of change. The first answer wins: an approval already settled is a `conflict`, and one past its time limit stays denied. Only the board page calls this, with the person's cookie; an agent that calls it is refused with `forbidden`. It returns the `approval_result` event.

200.description: The settled approval, as its event.

get.description: Stream a session's chat events as server-sent `chat` events, each with its `seq` as the event id: first every event after `after`, then each new one as it happens. A client that reconnects passes the last `seq` it saw. Only the board page calls this, with the person's cookie; an agent that calls it is refused with `forbidden`. The connection stays open until the client closes it.

post.summary: Ask the person before a file change or command
post.description: Tell the server, as facts, what the agent is about to change (a file write) or run (a shell command), and wait until it is settled. Only the gate hook of a running chat session calls this, with that session's run token; the person's cookie is refused with `forbidden`. The person is asked unless an answer kept for the session decides; silence past the time limit, a Stop or a new message is a denial. It returns `approved`, and how it was settled.

get.description: Show the folder the board server has open: its absolute path, its name as the person reads it (starting with `~` under the home folder), whether it has a Vision Board and how many boards that holds. Every other operation reads and writes this folder's ledger. Only the board page calls this, with the person's cookie; an agent that calls it is refused with `forbidden`.

post.description: Open another folder under the home folder in place of the one open now, on the same server and port. The server takes the folder's lock first and changes nothing if it can't; then it stops every running chat, ends every live stream (so every open page reloads onto the new folder), lets go of the old folder's lock, and keeps the folder in the recent list. A folder with no Vision Board is refused with `not-found` unless `create` is true, which makes `.visionboard/` and an empty ledger there. Agents join again after a switch: each folder keeps its own agents, so an old secret gets `not-authenticated`. Only the board page calls this, with the person's cookie; an agent that calls it is refused with `forbidden`. It returns the folder now open.

open.summary: Open a folder that has a Vision Board

create.summary: Create a Vision Board in a folder and open it

get.summary: List folders under the home folder
get.description: List one folder under the home folder (the home folder itself when `path` is left out): whether it has a Vision Board and how many boards, the folders in it, each marked when it has one, and the folders opened lately. On the home folder's listing it adds `places`, the cloud storage folders (`~/Library/CloudStorage`, when that folder exists) under their real names, each checked like any other folder. Folder names only: never a file's name or contents, never a hidden folder, `node_modules` or a link. A path outside the home folder, or reached through a hidden folder, is refused with `forbidden`. Only the board page calls this, with the person's cookie; an agent that calls it is refused with `forbidden`.

200.description: The folder and the folders in it.

agentSecret.description: The secret `join` returned, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`.

personCookie.name: vb_person
personCookie.description: Set by the server when it serves the board page; the page sends it.

runToken.description: The run token the server gives one chat session's gate hook, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It opens only the gate's route, and only while that session runs.

boardQuery.name: board
boardQuery.description: Keep only this board's lines (lines that name only a node are matched through the node's board).

after.name: after
after.description: A ledger `seq`: return what came after it. 0 (the default) means from the start. Pass the `head` you last saw.

limit.name: limit
limit.description: How many to return at most (default 100, at most 500).

wait.name: wait
wait.description: Seconds (0-60) to hold the call until the person presses Send or answers a request. 0 answers at once.

linked.name: linked
linked.description: True also returns the nodes linked to this one.

sessionPath.name: session
sessionPath.description: The chat session id, from start_chat or list_chats.

approvalPath.name: approval
approvalPath.description: The approval id, from its approval_request event.

chatAfter.name: after
chatAfter.description: A chat event's `seq`: stream what came after it. 0 (the default) replays the session from the start.

folderQuery.name: path
folderQuery.description: A folder under the home folder, as list_folders or get_project gave it; left out, the home folder.

projectHeader.name: VB-Project
projectHeader.description: The folder you work in, as an absolute path percent-encoded the way `encodeURI` does it (the `vb` MCP server sends it on every call). When the board server has another folder open, and this folder is not that one or inside it, the call is refused with `wrong-folder` and nothing is read or written. Left out, nothing is checked.

badRequest.description: The request cannot be read: not JSON, a bad id in the path, or a bad query.

example.title: Bad request
example.detail: The board id in the path is not valid. Use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, up to 64, not starting with a hyphen.

notAuthenticated.description: The Bearer secret is missing or unknown.

example.title: Not authenticated
example.detail: The server does not know this secret. Call join again, then request_grant for each container you need; the person must approve again.

forbidden.description: The Host or Origin is not allowed, or the wrong kind of caller used this route.

example.title: Forbidden
example.detail: Only the person can do this, on the board; send a propose or reply item instead.

notFound.description: No such board, node or region.

example.title: Not found
example.detail: There is no board "pricing". Call list_boards to see the boards.

methodNotAllowed.description: The path exists but not for this method.

tooLarge.description: The body or the batch is over the limit.

example.title: Too large
example.detail: The body is over the 64 KiB limit. Split the items across several calls.

invalid.description: The body fails the schema or a context rule.

example.title: Invalid
example.detail: The request does not fit the schema. Fix the fields listed in errors and send it again.

serverError.description: Something unexpected; the detail is in the server log, not here.

example.title: Server error
example.detail: Something went wrong on the server. Try again; if it keeps failing, tell the person.

chatNotFound.description: No such board, chat session or approval.

example.title: Not found
example.detail: There is no chat session "3f1c2a9e-5b7d-4e21-9a0c-6d8e2f4b1a37" on this server. Call list_chats to see the board's sessions.

chatConflict.description: The session is busy, or the approval is already settled.

example.title: Conflict
example.detail: The agent is still answering the last message. Wait for it, or press Stop.

folderForbidden.description: The folder is outside the home folder or hidden, or the wrong kind of caller used this route.

example.title: Forbidden
example.detail: Only folders under your home folder can be opened, and not hidden ones. Choose a folder under ~.

folderNotFound.description: No such folder, or (open_project without `create`) no Vision Board in it.

example.title: Not found
example.detail: No Vision Board here: ~/projects/new-app has no .visionboard/ledger.jsonl. Send create: true to make one, or choose another folder.

folderConflict.description: Another board server holds the folder's ledger, or its ledger could not be made or read; the open folder is unchanged.

example.title: Conflict
example.detail: Another board server holds this ledger: computer "example-laptop", process 4242, port 4466, running since 2026-10-09T09:00:00.000Z. Stop that server first.

wrongFolder.description: The board server has another folder open: the `VB-Project` header names a different folder, or the secret belongs to an agent of a folder opened before. Nothing was read or written. Stop and tell the person; do not join here.

example.title: Wrong folder
example.detail: The board has switched to ~/projects/b. Your work is in ~/projects/a. Ask the person to open it again; don't join here.
